1.

The present claim petition is based on Detailed Accident Report (DAR) filed under section 166 clause (4) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred to as Act) by the investigating officer of FIR No.122/2018 Police Station Mandawali, Delhi.

The case of the petitioner is that the accident in Omwati Gautam vs . Sohaib Anis & Ors on 21 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/122811166/
1 the present case took place on 22.04.2018, at around 06.15 AM, at Akshardham Games Village,
Delhi.

entities.text: Omwati Gautam vs . Sohaib Anis & Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As per FIR, the petitioner namely Omwati was on her morning walk near Akshardham Khelgaon and when she was on road, a car ("offending vehicle") came from behind and hit the petitioner from backside while being driven at a very high speed and in a rash and negligent manner.
She fell down on the road and sustained injuries and she had fallen unconscious.
Thereafter, she was taken to the hospital.

During investigation, it is found that the said offending vehicle was being driven in rash and negligence manner by respondent No.1 and being owned by respondent No.2 and the number of the said vehicle is DL-9CAF-7010.
2.
After service of respondents, all the respondents have marked appearance.
Respondents No. 1 and 2 have filed their joint written statement.
In their written statement, they have stated that they have nothing to do with the accident and no accident took place as alleged by the petitioner.
The vehicle of respondent No. 2 was implicated in this case and the same was duly insured and R-1 was having valid driving license.
3. Respondent No 3 / insurer had given legal offer which was not accepted by the petitioner and hence matter proceeded for evidence.

4. On the basis of the pleadings of the parties following issues were framed on 17.02.2021 :-
i.
Whether the petitioner is entitled to compensation on account of said injuries and if yes, to what extent and from whom?(OPP).
ii. Whether the petitioner is entitled to interest on the award amount, if so, at what rate and for which period?
(OPP).
5. In order to establish her claim, petitioner Omwati who is the injured has examined herself as PW1.
She has relied upon the copy of FIR, chargesheet, her MLC, medical bills and prescription and other documents in support of her claim.
6. Respondent side opted not to lead evidence.

7. I have heard Sh. Binod Kumar Jha, counsel for petitioners and Mr. Rajesh Goel, counsel for no.
3/insurer and perused the record.
Whether the petitioner is entitled to compensation on account of said injuries and if yes, to what extent and from whom?(OPP).

8. At the outset, it is relevant to mention that vide order dated 17.02.2021, while framing the issues,
it was mentioned in the order passed by the Tribunal that "It is observed that on the basis (sic) legal offer of insurance company, an interim award of Rs.65,000/- alongwith 9% interest has already been passed vide order dated 15.10.2019.

In view of this, the facts related to the cause of accident,
involvement of offending vehicle and the grievous nature of injuries suffered by petitioner are not in dispute".

This finding of the Tribunal was not challenged before any Appellate forum and has Omwati Gautam vs . Sohaib Anis & Ors on 21 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/122811166/
2 attained finality.

entities.text: Omwati Gautam vs . Sohaib Anis & Ors on 21 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus, the only question which remains to be decided is the entitlement of compensation on account of injuries sustained in the accident in question and to what extent petitioner is entitled for compensation and whom the duty be cast to pay the amount of compensation.
9. Section 168 of the Act enjoins the Claims Tribunal to hold an inquiry into the claim to make an award determining the amount of compensation which appears to it to be just and reasonable.
It has to be borne in mind that the compensation is not expected to be a windfall or a bonanza nor it should be pittance.

MEDICAL EXPENSES:
10. The petitioner has placed on record medical bills Ex.PW1/6 and discharge summary from Max hospital dated 17.05.2018 mark A, she has also filed photocopies of certain medical bills which are mark C and original prescription dated 15.09.2018 which is Ex. PW1/8.

During her cross-examination, PW1 / petitioner admitted that her husband is entitled to medial reimbursement from CGHS and that the bill relating to her hospitalization in Max Hospital was paid by Delhi Arogya Kosh.
She has also admitted that original discharge summary and final bills of Max Hospital were sent to CGHS for reimbursement.

At the stage of final arguments, Learned counsel for petitioner has also filed the letter from AAO/CAU/Hort., DDA showing that the claim in sum of Rs.36,026/- against the claim submitted for Rs.39,520/-for the period from15.04.2018 to 17.05.2018 was the admissible amount as per CGHS / DDA medical scheme.

Three Medicine bills of Apollo Pharmacy (part of Ex. PW1/6) are on record but a careful perusal of these bills show that only one of these medicine bills (page No.1 of Ex. PW1/6) is original i.e. dated 2018- 09-12 for a sum of Rs.2,800/- and the other two are photocopy / carbon copy.
No explanation has come forward regarding the missing original bills.
Respondent No. 3 has not taken the plea that the bill dated 2018-09-12 was also reimbursed, even though it pertains to September 2018.
Further, one bill of Dental Imaging Centre of Rs.500/- is also on record (page No.5 of Ex. PW1/6) for a sum of Rs.500/-.

Page No.6 of the Ex. PW1/6 is photostat of Max Healthcare bill for Rs.150/- and original of it is not proved on record and from the testimony of petitioner and absence of original, it appears that this bill as well as bills of Apollo Pharmacy (page No.2 & 3 of document Ex. PW1/6) are already reimbursed.

Even otherwise, I am of the view that in the absence of any explanation of the missing original and any prayer for leading of secondary evidence, the photostat copies cannot be considered by the court.
However, I am of the view that bill at page No.1 and 5 of Ex. PW1/6 requires to be compensated for by the court.

No other original medical bills have been filed or proved on record,
except the papers relating to Sarin Dental care (page No.4 of Ex.PW1/6), which is being dealt with in succeeding paragraphs.
11. Learned counsel for petitioner has laid stress on the documents Ex. PW1/7 and submits that the original of this is already a part of document Ex.PW1/6.
I have gone through both of the documents which are in original and by no stretch of imagination, one can be called as the duplicate or original of another.

Learned counsel for petitioner further explained that as bill dated 09.10.2018 (page no.4 of document Ex.PW1/6) was unclear on the point of treatment undertaken and with respect to which of the teeth and the expenses incurred over the same, details were sought from Sarin Dental Omwati Gautam vs . Sohaib Anis & Ors on 21 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/122811166/
3

entities.text: Sarin Dental Omwati Gautam vs . Sohaib Anis & Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Care and document Ex. PW1/7 was issued.
It is seen that the document Ex.PW1/7 is dated 08.09.2022 whereas the purported "receipt" in question dated is 09.10.2018.

No witness from Sarin Dental Care was examined to explain these documents and from the documents it cannot be determined that the treatment undergone in Sarin Dental Care was only with respect to the teeth related injuries sustained in the accident in question.

Here, it cannot be lost sight of that during her cross-examination, PW1 admitted having got dental treatment for decay and caries in teeth in Sarin Dental Care also for several other teeth, other than the 3 teeth from upper jaw as lost in the accident.
She deposed that "It is correct that I had lost 3 teeth from upper jaw but I got RCT done and the crowns fixed in several other teeth which had decayed and carries (sic)".
Document Ex. PW1/7

is post-dated document and in the absence of the examination of any witness from Sarin Dental Care,
the chances of manipulation cannot be ruled out.

There is nothing in the testimony of PW1 to suggest that apart from 3 front upper jaw teeth, there was any other dental injury sustained by her,
as warranting the extensive treatment as reflected in document Ex. PW1/4.

There is nothing in her testimony to suggest either that due to the impact of accident, any other existing teeth of her or jaw was affected or she sustained an overall injury, as involving entire teeth on lower and upper jaws.
Hence, the document Ex.PW1/7 cannot be taken on its face value.
It is noteworthy to mention that treatment taking in Sarin Dental Care was at a later stage and not during the period of two hospitalizations post accident in Max Hospital.

A careful perusal of document at page 4 of Ex.
PW1/6 shows that no description or reference of accident is made in this document and further there is nothing in this document to show what all treatment was given to petitioner only with respect to the dental related injuries sustained in the accident and there is no argument advanced by Learned counsel for petitioner as co-relate the treatments at Max Hospital, MLC and treatment at Sarin Dental Care as a whole.

Further, petitioner has not even placed on record proof regarding payment of Rs.1,20,000/- to Sarin Dental Care on 09.10.2018 or that the same was only for the dental treatment with respect to the dental injuries sustained in the accident.

During oral arguments, it was submitted by Learned counsel for petitioner that no proper and complete dental treatment of the missing teeth was undertaken in Max Hospital and though respondent has disputed this, it is not the claim of the respondent No.3 that cosmetic dental treatment was also undertaken in Max hospital and paid for by department of husband of petitioner.
12.

While MLC reflects that three teeth of petitioner were found missing (without adverting to if it was as a result of fresh injuries) and there was history of oral bleeding present, petitioner herself has deposed in her examination-in-chief that only two of her teeth were broken in accident.

Whatever may be the case, it is obvious from the medical documents of Max hospital read with testimony of petitioner that she suffered from dental injury and her teeth were broken and further that she had facial fracture.
Document Ex. PW1/8 is a photocopy.

Tribunal is not oblivious to the fact that in reply to the notice of IO under section 91 of Code of Criminal Procedure, it is mentioned on behalf of Max Super Specialty hospital that reduction of facial fracture Maxilla was done in second hospitalization.

It cannot be lost sight of that losing teeth may require to be restored through cosmetic treatment and it also involves pain /sensitivity as requiring necessary processes and correctional measures by the dentist.

Hence, even though petitioner has not proved any proper bill of Sarin Dental Care as reflecting the mode of payment, serial number and details regarding injuries sustained in the accident and that the treatment undertaken was solely as a result of and directly related to the road traffic accident injuries, the receipt in question at page No.4 of Ex. PW1/6 at least Omwati Gautam vs . Sohaib Anis & Ors on 21 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/122811166/
4 ex-facie shows that dental treatment was taken and this must have involved the teeth lost in the accident, even though the petitioner underwent dental treatment for pre-existing caries and teeth not affected by accident.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Hence, it can be safely assumed that medical expenses in sum of Rs.
40,000/- was required / incurred for dental injuries in the accident.
13. Hence, I consider it proper to award a sum of Rs.43,300/- (2,800 +500+40,000) under this head.

PAIN AND SUFFERING:
14.
The treatment record / medical documents are Ex. PW1/6 and Mark A placed on record by the petitioner.

Perusal of the discharge summary mark A and MLC Ex. PW1/5 reflects that after the accident the petitioner was taken to Max Hospital on 22.04.2018, where her MLC was prepared and she was diagnosed with Anterior falx and left frontal region with multiple facial fracture and she was given treatment and was discharged on 29.04.2018.

Further, photocopy of another discharge summary (part of DAR) shows that petitioner was again admitted to Max Hospital on 15.05.2018 and she was given treatment "Reduction of Facial Fracture Maxilla" and was discharged on 17.05.2018.

Further, the reply sent to the IO, PS Mandawali to the notice under section 91 Cr. PC by the Max Super Specialty Hospital, Patparganj, Delhi (part of DAR) shows that the petitioner lastly visited the hospital on 24.07.2018 and she was hospitalized twice for her treatment.

Ex.PW1/8,
photocopy of a prescription is dated 15.09.2018 which shows her further treatment.
Further, MLC of the petitioner also gave impression "missing three teeth from upper jaw".
In view of this, it is clear the petitioner must have remained under immense pain and suffering for a long time during her treatment.
Though the petitioner has claimed in her testimony that she was on complete bed rest for about 6 months, no medical document in support of this claim has been placed on record.
In view of above above-said discussion, this court finds it appropriate to award the petitioner Rs. 25,000/- as compensation under this head.

LOSS OF INCOME (DURING TREATMENT):
15.

As mentioned above, the petitioner had to remain hospitalized twice since the date of accident i.e. 22.04.2018 and first she was hospitalized from 22.04.2018 to 29.04.2018 and again from 15.05.2018 to 17.05.2018 and thus she remained in hospital for 11 days.

Though in her examination-in-chief, she deposed that she was self-employed and was earning Rs.20,000/- per month, however, she has not mentioned the nature of her work and in support of her claim, she has not placed on record any document relating to occupation and income.
During her cross-examination, she stated that she was not earning anything before the accident.
Hence, it is clear that petitioner was homemaker and averment in para no.10 of affidavit Ex. PW1/A is false.
She is stated to have lost teeth and undergone facial fracture and other injuries.
In view of above, it can be safely assumed that petitioner was not able to do her work for about 3 months.

16. While discussing the issue of loss of earning by a homemaker, various judicial pronouncement have established the proposition of law that contribution of a homemaker to the household and society at large cannot be ignored and a notional income of a homemaker has to be fixed by the Omwati Gautam vs . Sohaib Anis & Ors on 21 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/122811166/
5

entities.text: Omwati Gautam vs . Sohaib Anis & Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Tribunal while deciding the issue of compensation on account of loss of income during treatment and the said notional income, in a given set of facts and circumstances has to be just and neither high nor low.

In Jitendra Khimshankar Trivedi v. Kasam Daud Kumbhar, (2015) 4 SCC 237, the Supreme Court has observed that:
"10. Even assuming Jayvantiben Jitendra Trivedi was not self-employed doing embroidery and tailoring work, the fact remains that she was a housewife and a homemaker.

entities.text: Jitendra Khimshankar Trivedi v. Kasam Daud Kumbhar, (2015) 4 SCC 237
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is hard to monetise the domestic work done by a house- mother.
The services of the mother/wife is available 24 hours and her duties are never fixed.
Courts have recognised the contribution made by the wife to the house is invaluable and that it cannot be computed in terms of money.

A housewife/homemaker does not work by the clock and she is in constant attendance of the family throughout and such services rendered by the homemaker has to be necessarily kept in view while calculating the loss of dependency.
Thus even otherwise, taking deceased Jayvantiben Jitendra Trivedi as the homemaker, it is reasonable to fix her income at Rs 3000 per month."

17. Further, in National Insurance Co. Ltd. vs Chitra and Ors, in MAC. APP. 1056/2016 decided on 13.07.2023, Delhi High Court, while upholding the decision of the Tribunal (Tribunal had awarded the compensation to Petitioner/injured lady -who had not been able to prove that she was earning member of the family- taking the minimum wages of a graduate in order to calculate the loss of income), observed that "10...only because the respondent no. 1 was a homemaker, her contribution to the household cannot be undermined.

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd. vs Chitra and Ors, in MAC. APP. 1056/2016
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: She contributed in her own ways to the household.
As a homemaker she would be expected to do physical housework, apart from giving emotional and other support to the family members..."
18. In the case at hand, during her cross-examination, petitioner stated that she is illiterate.
The petitioner is stated to be the resident of Delhi.

Though no document regarding residential proof of the petitioner is placed on record, however, present matter is the DAR case filed by the Investigating Officer after verification and in the DAR the address of the petitioner is mentioned as of Delhi.

In view of the fact that petitioner was illiterate, aged about 64 years as on 07.09.2021 (date of verification of affidavit is Ex. PW1/A) and aged 55 years on the date of accident ( as per MLC EX.
PW1/5 and the age of the petitioner is not disputed by respondents) and was the resident of Delhi at time of accident, the Tribunal consider it proper that her income is considered on the basis of minimum wages applicable to the unskilled category at the relevant time in Delhi.
The minimum rates of wages under that category at the relevant time of accident was Rs.13,896/- per month.
19. As discussed above, the treatment of petitioner continued till July 2018 i.e. for 3 months at least after the accident.
20. In view of above, petitioner is granted a sum of Rs.41,688/- (Rs.13,896x3) on account of loss of income during treatment.
Thus, the petitioner is granted a sum of Rs. 41,688/- under this head.

Omwati Gautam vs . Sohaib Anis & Ors on 21 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/122811166/
6 CONVEYANCE, ATTENDANT & SPECIAL DIET CHARGES:
21.

entities.text: Omwati Gautam vs . Sohaib Anis & Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Though no evidence has come on record to prove the expenses incurred by the petitioner on the conveyance, however, considering that the petitioner remained hospitalized twice and her treatment continued till July 2018, an inference can be drawn that family members of petitioner had to spend considerable amount to visit hospital number of times during the treatment of the petitioner and she must have spent reasonable amount for his special diet for the purpose of early recovery post surgery.
Thus, the petitioner is granted a sum of Rs.5,000/- towards conveyance and special diet.
22. Though in her evidence, PW1 / petitioner has deposed that she engaged Maid for household work for six months @ 10,000/- per month and spent Rs.60,000/- for maid.
However, no documents in support of her claim has been placed on record.

Rather, such a claim made by her in her examination-in-chief, comes up as false during her cross-examination where she deposed that she had not employed any attendant for looking after her after the accident and no amount of money was paid to her relatives / family members who looked after post accident.

Still, it cannot be ignored that family members of the petitioner must had to render their services for providing assistance to the petitioner in her routine activities and that was bound to suffer their work / job.

For claiming compensation, necessity of employing a professional attendant / care taker is not required and the petitioner should be compensated for the value of services of the family members,
which has been or would be necessitated by the wrong doing of the driver.

(Refer : DTC & Ors Vs.
Lalita, 1983 ACJ 253).
In view of above, a sum of Rs.5,000/- is awarded to petitioner as attendant charges.
23. Thus, a total sum of Rs.10,000/- (5,000+5,000) is awarded to the petitioner under this head.

24. Thus, the compensation awarded to the petitioner is summarized as under:-
 Sl. No. Head of compensation Amount  1. Medical Expenses Rs. 43,300/-
 2. Pain & Suffering Rs. 25,000/-
 Loss of income (during Rs. 41,688./-
 3.
 treatment)
 Conveyance, Attendant and Rs. 10,000/-
 4.
 Special Diet expenses
TOTAL Rs

25. On perusal of record, it is reflected that interim award to the tune of Rs.65,000/- was passed in favour of the petitioner vide order dated 15.10.2019 and the same was ordered to be released to the petitioner in her bank account vide order dated 05.12.2019.

Therefore, while calculating the total Omwati Gautam vs . Sohaib Anis & Ors on 21 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/122811166/
7 compensation amount, the said interim award amount may be adjusted.

entities.text: Omwati Gautam vs . Sohaib Anis & Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
26. In view of above, the total compensation comes out to be Rs.55,000/- (1,20,000/- - 65,000/-).
LIABILITY 27.
Now, the question arises as to which of the respondents is liable to pay the compensation amount.

As insurance company has contractual and statutory liability to indemnify the insured and in this case, insurance company has not been able to prove that any term or condition of insurance policy was breached/violated by insured, therefore, respondent no.3/insurance company becomes liable to pay the aforesaid compensation amount.

ISSUE No.2 :
28.
The petitioner has conducted the proceedings in her case diligently.
Therefore, she is entitled for interest @ 7% per annum on the aforesaid award amount from the date of filing of the petition till date of realization.

RELIEF:
29.

In view of the findings on said issues, this Tribunal awards a total compensation of Rs.55,000/-
(rupees fifty five Thousand Only) alongwith interest @ 7% per annum w.e.f. date of filing of the petition till the date of its realization, in favour of petitioner and against the respondent no. 3 /
insurer and same is required to be deposited with this Tribunal within 30 days.
Announced in the open (Mayuri Singh)
